title: Close the transitive/delegated agent-config trust surface
acceptance: a PR that edits ONLY a file referenced by a floored agent-config (opencode.json/.jsonc instructions:[...] paths or globs, or an instruction-bearing prompt {file:./path}, or a CLAUDE.md @import) is graded at or above the referencing config's floor, not the default floor

reference targets are resolved deterministically from committed bytes at the canonical fork point (merge-base), never the PR head and never a scanner/heuristic; a PR cannot add or remove a reference to self-grade

CLAUDE.md @import resolution follows the first-party rule (code.claude.com/docs/en/memory): every relative import (bare, ./, ../) resolves relative to the directory of the CONTAINING file, not repo-root and not the working directory; recursion capped at four hops with cycle detection; code spans, fenced blocks, and backtick-literal `@x` are skipped; a relative import that escapes the repo root (via ..) is provably outside and skipped, but in-repo parent references (@../sibling) are NOT dropped; filesystem-absolute and ~-home imports FAIL CLOSED (verify blocks) because their repo-relative target is not derivable from committed bytes and skipping would be fail-open for an absolute path that resolves back inside the checkout (P2-1)

fail closed: if a floored config's reference directives cannot be parsed at the trusted ref, verify blocks (never silently passes a referenced file at a lower tier); a {file:...} outside instruction-bearing fields (e.g. a provider apiKey) does NOT floor; and an absolute or ~-home path in an opencode instructions entry or an instruction-field {file:} FAILS CLOSED (blocks), matching the claude-md @import rule, since its repo-relative target is not derivable from committed bytes and skipping is fail-open when it resolves back into the checkout (P1)

instruction-bearing {file:} fields are agent.*.prompt, deprecated mode.*.prompt, AND command.*.template (a command template is the prompt sent to the LLM - opencode.ai/docs/commands - so {file:docs/steer.md} in it floors docs/steer.md; cross-family red-team Repro 1). Explicitly OUT of QRM-3.4 (-> QRM-4.0 residual): the command-prompt @file include is a distinct, repo-ROOT-relative mechanism spanning command.*.template and .opencode/commands/**/*.md (cross-family red-team Repro 2); QRM-3.4 does NOT claim to close it

opencode instructions entries and instruction-bearing {file:} paths resolve relative to the CONTAINING config file's directory (first-party opencode.ai/docs/config#files), NOT repo-root: a nested packages/a/opencode.jsonc with {file:prompts/review.md} floors packages/a/prompts/review.md (not prompts/review.md); glob instructions floor via the glob set; remote-URL instruction entries (http/https, which opencode allows) are skipped as non-repo (P1)

the committed policy ANNOTATES every known reference-bearing floor with its reference_extractor (**/CLAUDE.md and **/CLAUDE.local.md -> claude-md; **/opencode.json and **/opencode.jsonc -> opencode-json); a floored reference-bearing rule that omits the annotation resolves no references and is the same under-floor class as an unknown value; a mechanical policy-lint that fails validation on a known reference-bearing glob lacking its extractor is banked as a follow-up (P2, principle 2)

a fail-closed block emits an actionable diagnostic: source config path, location (line or JSON pointer), extractor type, offending token, reason (absolute / home / unparseable), and portable remediation (use a repo-relative path) (P3)

reference matching and floor computation go through ONE shared code path: a single isReferencedPath(path, referencedFloors) feeds both the computeTierFloor reference contribution and the computeUncoveredPaths exempt-override, and both cmdVerify and cmdTier compute the floor via one shared resolver so tier cannot drift onto the 2-arg pure path (P2/P3)
no over-broad flooring: only the actually-referenced paths (or a referenced directory/glob) enter the floor set, not their whole directories

enforcement consistency: both cmdVerify and cmdTier resolve references by default so `tier` reports what the gate enforces (QRM-3.2 guarantee); a referenced path requires coverage even if it matches exempt_paths

Cursor rule references are explicitly DEFERRED from v1: .cursor/**, .cursorrules, .cursorignore remain floored directly (the config files are covered); only transitive references from a .mdc rule to a non-.cursor file are out of scope, pending first-party sourcing of the Cursor reference grammar (tracked follow-up). Deferral is documented in docs/handoffs/QRM-3.4-design.md, and QRM-4.0.json carries the Cursor .mdc residual as its own delegated-reference prerequisite so closing QRM-3.4 does NOT mark that prerequisite satisfied (P2-2)

this is a QRM-4.0 Gate prerequisite: the Gate is not complete tier-floor enforcement while a floor can be bypassed by delegation. It also surfaces a NEW QRM-4.0 prerequisite -- authenticated-forge tree listing (listFiles at the trusted ref) so references resolve in forge mode -- now RECORDED in .quorum/manifests/QRM-4.0.json (P2-3), not left implicit
